content.rendered:
“Gloria” is a riff-rock classic that’s perfectly suited for the E Street Band’s guitar-heavy arsenal. It’s turned up in Bruce’s setlist more than a dozen times over the years, and that’s not including its frequent mini-appearance as a lead-in to “She’s the One.” It’s clearly a significant song for Bruce, as you can hear in this conversation between Bruce and Steve from the Underground Garage in 2011.

Bruce may have bought the single on instinct, but as he says as above, “When that hit, once that hit, if you couldn’t play it, you didn’t get a gig.”

So play it they did. There are plenty of video clips to choose from, but I’m partial to this one from a few years ago–it’s nice and close up, with great audio.

Here’s the original 1964 B-side(!) by Them.

Gloria
First performed: December 26, 1975 (New York City, NY)
Last performed: May 1, 2014 (Tampa, FL)

© March 16, 2018

jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce and Nicky Addeo and the Night Owls croon a soulful cover of "What's Your Name?" at the Stone Pony.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce makes his first guest appearance with Patti Smith, and Patti Scialfa misses her first Broadway show with Bruce.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hippy Hippy Shake
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: From the Legends of Springsteen files: Bruce and Max join cover band Stand and Deliver at the Classics Cafe in Westwood for rocking rendition of "Hippy Hippy Shake."

jetpack-related-posts.title: Good Lovin’
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: It took more than four decades for Bruce to cover "Good Lovin'," but he made up for it when he did. Great performances inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Slow Down
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce covers Larry Williams' influential "Slow Down" with a cover band at the Classics Cafe in Westwood, New Jersey.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Let’s Go, Let’s Go, Let’s Go
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Days after Hank Ballard's passing, Bruces Springsteen and Hornsby (along with former Steel Mill bandmate Robbin Thompson) pay tribute by playing Ballard's last great hit.
